title: Bending reality with Gaussian splats and VR
cardTitle: Bending reality with Gaussian splats and VR
summary: A VR experiment in making people question what they see. We used a scanned hallway and Codex to turn familiar surroundings into an impossible space.
coverAlt: Calibrated VR experience with a scanned hallway and shifting geometry

metadata.label: My role
metadata.value: Experience direction, spatial interaction and AI-assisted prototyping

metadata.label: Tools
metadata.value: Codex, Gaussian splats, WebXR, Three.js, Meta Quest 3, SteamVR / Steam Link

blocks.title: A familiar space made unreliable
blocks.body: We wanted to bend reality until participants could no longer trust their eyes. Could we do it without modelling the environment or writing the code ourselves? Gaussian splats gave us the captured space; Codex helped turn our directions into interactions.

blocks.title: Designing through conversation with Codex
blocks.body: I described the behaviour, tested the result, and used annotated screenshots to explain what needed to change. Each iteration made the instructions more specific: what should move, what should stay fixed, and when the illusion should unfold.

items.title: 01 / Alignment
items.body: We used controller landmarks to align the scan with the physical space. A believable starting point gave the later distortions something to break.

items.title: 02 / Interaction
items.body: Manual buttons let me test box placement and hallway rotation before adding automatic triggers. The physical props stayed anchored while the virtual space moved.

items.title: 03 / Refinement
items.body: When the collapsing hallway looked too neatly cut, I asked Codex for uneven patches of disappearing splats. Visual feedback shaped the effect, timing and transitions.

blocks.label: Three stages of prototyping with Codex

blocks.title: Screenshots as prompts
blocks.body: I drew directly on screenshots to show Codex where to cut and how the spaces should connect. These behind-the-scenes images became instructions for the next iteration. Prompts below are condensed from the original conversations.

items.alt: Screenshot sent to Codex with red markings defining the hallway section to extract
items.label: Prompt: Extract this section as a separate splat, with cuts perpendicular to the walls and floor. Keep the existing interactions and positions unchanged.

items.alt: Screenshot sent to Codex with handwritten floor and orientation labels around the opening
items.label: Prompt: Connect the hallway cutout to this opening. Match its floor, ceiling and walls to the marked edges, and keep it attached to the hole.

blocks.title: Disorientation from two perspectives
blocks.body: We recorded both the VR view and what participants were doing in the physical space. This let us compare what they saw with how they moved and reacted.

blocks.title: Participant reactions
blocks.body: Participants described the experience as very disorienting, compared it to Inception, and called it amazing. Their reactions echoed our intention: to make a familiar space feel impossible and leave people questioning what their eyes were telling them.
